rule: Glyphs of one shared size sit in a top row, each with its own colour and touching all four sides of its bounding box. Below them, the interior of a single-colour frame is a coarse grid of cells, each (interior size / glyph size). A few whole cells are painted in one fill colour, and they are consistent with exactly one glyph. The output is the cropped frame with that glyph drawn at cell scale: fill colour where the glyph is filled, background where it is empty.
scope: Fresh full-bounding-box glyphs with near-mutated distractors, positive coarse-cell hint conjunctions, unique target selection and frame-cropped scaled completion. Varies glyph shape, non-square cell scales, colours, positions and margins.
constraints: Four unchanged canonical pairs reconstructed exactly.
1240 unique independently decoded puzzles: 794 require multiple hints jointly, 940 have close distractors, 1124 have disconnected glyphs, 352 use non-square cells and 139 use zero as fill colour.
40 dense-control trials retain six 3x3 glyphs and six hints; 40 each exercise unit cells, six-pixel cells, alternate palette, single hints and non-square cells.
Reject malformed glyph rows, colour/column/hint containers and noninteger optional explicit controls with ValueError.
Distractor construction excludes target supersets that make every possible positive hint ambiguous, before expensive scene retries.
Final critic parameter proposals: 21 successes and 9 expected rejections.
known_limitations: Glyphs remain in an upper row and the frame below; mixed glyph sizes, partial hint cells, multiple fill colours and lateral frame layouts are outside native support.
One-hint requests intentionally provide easier single-cell identification.
Glyph and hint sizes must stay smaller than the frame border and the background strictly dominates; these inference guards restrict dense layouts.
Random shapes/sizes may be resampled when scene-level constraints fail; no claim of a uniform distribution over feasible geometry.

authored_scope: Random mode samples 3x3, 4x3 and 3x4 glyphs (fixture shapes) and 4x4 glyphs (synthetic). It uses 2..5 glyphs (2..6 on request), cell sizes 2..4 per axis (1 and 5..6 on request, synthetic; non-square cells synthetic), and 2..4 hint cells (1..6 on request). It varies canvas size up to 30x30 along with glyph offsets, gaps, frame position, and frame, fill and glyph colours; bg defaults to 8. Distractors include close mutations of the target, and hint sets preferably have no single uniquely-identifying cell. Explicit mode reconstructs the fixtures exactly from latent parameters. Not supported: frame above or beside the glyphs, mixed glyph sizes, multiple fill colours, partial-cell hints.
authored_constraints: All glyphs share one size, are distinct, and touch all four sides of their bounding box; random glyphs are non-solid with at least 3 cells.
bg, frame colour, fill colour and every glyph colour are pairwise distinct ints 0..9.
Glyphs are separated by at least one background column, start at column >= 1 in random mode, and are separated from the frame by at least one blank row.
Hint cells are a proper subset of the target glyph and are not a subset of any other glyph, so the answer is unique.
Total hint area and every glyph's cell count are strictly smaller than the frame border, so the frame is the strictly largest single-colour object.
Background is strictly the most common colour in the input.
Frame interior dimensions are exact multiples of the glyph dimensions (by construction).
All scalar controls must be Python ints; bools and floats are rejected with ValueError.
Infeasible random-mode controls (geometry or hint area versus border) are rejected before sampling; sampling uses bounded retries (400 outer, 200/50/30 inner).
